entries.name: Data pipeline
entries.definition: An automated series of steps that moves data from its sources through processing to a destination such as a data warehouse.

entries.name: Data storage technologies
entries.definition: The hardware and software used to store digital data, such as disk arrays, flash storage, object storage and tape.

entries.name: Data Vault modeling
entries.definition: A data-warehouse modelling method, created by Dan Linstedt, that organises data into hubs, links and satellites so that history is kept and many sources can be integrated.

entries.name: Data visualization
entries.definition: Encoding data visually to support interpretation.

entries.name: Data warehouse management
entries.definition: Administering a data warehouse, including its data loading, storage, performance, security and availability.

entries.name: Data wrangling
entries.definition: Cleaning, reshaping and combining raw data so it can be analysed.

entries.name: Database administration
entries.definition: Installing, configuring, securing, backing up and tuning database systems so that they stay available and perform well.

entries.name: Database as a service
entries.definition: A cloud service model in which a provider runs and manages a database that customers use without managing the underlying servers.

entries.name: Database design
entries.definition: Designing database structures and constraints.

entries.name: Database life cycle
entries.definition: The stages a database passes through, from requirements and design to implementation, operation, maintenance and retirement.

entries.name: Database mirroring
entries.definition: Keeping a second, synchronised copy of a database on another server so that it can take over if the primary server fails.

entries.name: Database systems
entries.definition: The study of software systems that store, organise and query data, and of how they are designed and run.

entries.name: Database trigger
entries.definition: A stored routine that a database runs automatically when a defined event, such as an insert, update or delete, happens on a table.

entries.name: DB-Access
entries.definition: A command-line and menu-driven tool from IBM Informix for running SQL statements and managing Informix databases.

entries.name: DB2/400
entries.definition: The relational database built into IBM's AS/400 midrange systems, now called Db2 for i.

entries.name: DBCC
entries.definition: Database Console Commands, a set of Transact-SQL commands in Microsoft SQL Server for checking database consistency and doing maintenance and diagnostics.

entries.name: DbFit
entries.definition: An open-source tool, built on the FitNesse framework, for writing and running automated database tests as wiki tables.

entries.name: DBpedia
entries.definition: A community project that extracts structured data from Wikipedia and publishes it as linked open data that can be queried with SPARQL.

entries.name: dbSNP
entries.definition: A public database run by the US National Center for Biotechnology Information that catalogues single nucleotide polymorphisms and other short genetic variations.

entries.name: DbUnit
entries.definition: A JUnit extension for testing database-driven Java applications by loading known data sets and comparing database contents.

entries.name: DbVisualizer
entries.definition: A graphical database client for browsing, querying and administering many kinds of databases.

entries.name: dc.js
entries.definition: A JavaScript charting library, built on D3 and Crossfilter, for exploring multi-dimensional datasets with linked, interactive charts.

entries.name: DCID 6/3
entries.definition: Director of Central Intelligence Directive 6/3, a former US intelligence-community policy on securing information systems that handle sensitive compartmented information, later replaced by ICD 503.

entries.name: Deal shaping
entries.definition: Structuring the scope, price and terms of a commercial deal so that it suits both the customer and the company.

entries.name: Dealing with enquiries
entries.definition: Answering questions and requests from customers or the public by phone, email or in person.

entries.name: Debits and credits
entries.definition: The double-entry bookkeeping convention of recording each transaction as equal debit and credit entries in different accounts.

entries.name: Deboning
entries.definition: Cutting the bones out of meat, poultry or fish.

entries.name: Deburring
entries.definition: Removing the sharp edges or burrs left on metal or plastic parts after machining or cutting.

entries.name: Decision-making software
entries.definition: Software that helps people analyse options, criteria and likely outcomes in order to reach a decision.

entries.name: Decorating
entries.definition: Improving the look of a room, event or item by painting, papering or adding ornaments and furnishings.

entries.name: deegree
entries.definition: An open-source Java software for building spatial data infrastructures and OGC web services such as WMS and WFS.

entries.name: Deep learning
entries.definition: Developing models built from multiple neural-network layers.

entries.name: Defensive tactics
entries.definition: Techniques for defending oneself and for controlling and restraining a subject, taught to police and security staff.

entries.name: Deflashing
entries.definition: Removing the thin excess material, called flash, left on moulded or cast parts.

entries.name: Delivery pipeline
entries.definition: An automated sequence of build, test and deployment stages that carries a code change from commit to production.

entries.name: Dell Wyse thin clients
entries.definition: Small, low-maintenance terminals made by Dell (formerly Wyse Technology) that run their applications from a central server.

entries.name: Deltek Costpoint
entries.definition: Enterprise resource planning software from Deltek, used mainly by government contractors and project-based businesses for accounting, project costing and billing.

entries.name: Demolition
entries.definition: Safely tearing down buildings or other structures and clearing the debris.

entries.name: Dental plaque removal
entries.definition: Removing plaque, the soft bacterial film, from teeth by scaling and polishing.

entries.name: Dental records
entries.definition: Creating and maintaining patient charts, treatment histories and images in a dental practice.
